summary: When His Pharisee host is surprised that He skipped the ritual washing, Jesus pronounces woes on Pharisees and lawyers for clean outsides and neglected hearts.
key_insight: The Pharisee only “marveled” that Jesus had not washed; Luke records no word from him. Jesus answered what he was thinking, and every woe that follows exposes the same gap between a careful outside and a neglected inside. As Jesus asked, “Did not He who made the outside make the inside also?”
story: As Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee asked Him to dine with him, and Jesus went in and sat down to eat. The Pharisee marveled that He had not first washed before dinner.

The Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees make the outside of the cup and dish clean, but your inward part is full of greed and wickedness. Foolish ones! Did not He who made the outside make the inside also?” Let them give alms from what they had, He said, and all things would be clean to them.

Then came the woes. Woe to the Pharisees, who tithed mint and rue and every garden herb but passed by justice and the love of God: “These you ought to have done, without leaving the others undone.” Woe to them for loving the best seats in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces. Woe to them, for they were “like graves which are not seen,” and people walked over them without knowing it.

One of the lawyers spoke up: “Teacher, by saying these things You reproach us also.” Jesus answered, “Woe to you also, lawyers! For you load men with burdens hard to bear, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.”

Woe to them, He said, for building the tombs of the prophets their fathers had killed; by doing so they showed that they approved of their fathers’ deeds. The wisdom of God had said that He would send prophets and apostles and that some would be killed, and the blood of all the prophets, “from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah who perished between the altar and the temple,” would be required of this generation.
“Woe to you lawyers! For you have taken away the key of knowledge. You did not enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in you hindered.”

As He said these things, the scribes and the Pharisees began to assail Him vehemently and to cross-examine Him about many things, lying in wait to catch Him in something He might say, so that they might accuse Him.

scene.label: Mint and rue
scene.text: The Law commanded a tithe of grain, new wine and oil (Deuteronomy 14:22–23). The Pharisees extended it to the small herbs of the kitchen garden. Jesus does not fault that care; He faults the neglect of justice and the love of God that went with it.

scene.label: Seats and greetings
scene.text: In the synagogue the leading men sat at the front, facing the congregation. In the marketplace a teacher of the Law expected a respectful greeting that acknowledged his rank. Both were public honors, given where everyone could see.

scene.label: Unseen graves
scene.text: Touching a grave made a person unclean for seven days (Numbers 19:16), so graves were marked, probably with whitewash each spring before Passover, to warn pilgrims. An unmarked grave spread uncleanness to people who never knew it. Matthew records a different picture of the same danger: “whitewashed tombs” (Matthew 23:27).

scene.label: Abel to Zechariah
scene.text: Abel’s murder is the first in Genesis (4:8). Zechariah the son of Jehoiada was stoned “in the court of the house of the LORD” (2 Chronicles 24:21), and Chronicles stands last in the Hebrew Bible. From Abel to Zechariah meant every martyr from the first page to the last.

scene.label: Lawyers
scene.text: Luke’s lawyers are the scribes: experts who studied, copied and taught the Law of Moses and ruled on how it applied to daily life. That is why Jesus speaks to them of burdens laid on others and of the key to knowledge.

witnesses.luke: Only Luke records this dinner. He alone shows Jesus eating in a Pharisee’s home three times (7:36; 11:37; 14:1), and each meal becomes a lesson. Matthew records similar woes spoken in the temple during the last week (Matthew 23); Jesus may well have said such things more than once, and here they are spoken across a private table.

seeing.reveals: Jesus will not trade the truth for a polite dinner. He sees through clean cups and careful tithes to the heart, because the God who made the outside made the inside too, and He cares more for justice and love than for herbs.
seeing.living: It is possible to be exact about small duties and careless about justice and the love of God. Let Jesus’ woes search the inside of your own cup before you apply them to anyone else. Ask where your faith has become a weight you lay on others without lifting a finger to help them carry it.
seeing.ponder: If Jesus came to dinner at your house, what would He notice that your guests never see?

preaching.big_idea: God made the inside as well as the outside, and He looks first at the heart.
preaching.watch_for: Jesus pronounces six woes, three to the Pharisees and three to the lawyers. Just before this meal He had warned, “Take heed that the light which is in you is not darkness” (11:35); the dinner shows what that inner darkness looks like in religious people.
